tickets.title: `List.merge` doubles work on fixed lists with an undecidable comparison
tickets.body:
On a fixed list whose elements make the comparison stuck (a `if le x y` the checker can't decide), `List.merge` (crates/elab/src/std/List/Sort.sw:463) computes both branches of the `if`, so the work doubles per element (0.42 s at 7+7, from docs/history.md:104; not re-measured). Mutual recursion is now complete (3d73325), so the fix is possible: write merge as a mutually recursive pair (one function for each side that is currently ahead, so each recursive call is in a single branch and neither branch needs to be computed to unstick the other), then restate the sorting proofs that unfold it: `List.mergeLeHead` (Sort.sw:514), `List.mergeSorted` (Sort.sw:523), the `Perm` and length lemmas below them, and `List.pushRunSorted` (Sort.sw:544). `Text.linesFrom` (std/Text/Text.sw:77) and the min/max folds have the same shape but are rare; leave them out.

First step: write a benchmark input (merge of two fixed lists of symbolic elements, 7+7) and record its step count, so the before and after are comparable. Done when: merge is a mutually recursive pair, the Sort.sw proofs are restated and check, and the 7+7 case is measured again with the number in the ticket.

History: opened from the checker-evaluation work (docs/proposals/checker-evaluation.md:596); waited on mutual recursion.

tickets.title: Lifted `match` in a partial function and in the REPL gives E-MATCH-MOTIVE: resolve its draft there

A `match` nested in a definition is lifted to a helper (a draft) and resolved after elaboration. Repro (release binary, 21 Oct):
  def f (n: Nat): {Partial} Nat :=
    let r := match n with | 0 => 1 | Succ m => m
    if r == 3 then 0 else f (n + 1)
and, in `stitchwort repl`, `(match 2 with | 0 => 1 | Succ m => m) + 1`.

Scope: resolve drafts for (a) and (c), the two a user can hit. (b) may stay refused, with a message that says why (a data or ability declaration has nowhere to put the helper). tickets.title: Style: no space before `:` (`(x: Nat)`, like Scala/TS)
tickets.body:
**Style: no space before `:` in type annotations?** Consider making `(x: Nat)` / `def f (n: Nat): Nat` the default style instead of `(x : Nat)` (user, 19 Oct).

19 Oct analysis (Sonnet): recommends keeping spaces (option a). Evidence: all 335 .sw files use ` : ` (~2,665 lines); the lexer ignores whitespace around `:` (lexer.rs:344-348, `:=` is one token), so `x: T` already parses; Lean/Mathlib style guide requires spaces, Agda/Idris docs use them; Rust/Kotlin/TS use `x: T`. Switching would touch ~180 of 280 CLI snapshots and the printer (pretty.rs:264,267), with no formatter to hold the line. Options: (a) keep; (b) switch everywhere after a `stitchwort fmt` exists; (c) mixed (rejected); (d) accept both, document house style.

Matt (19 Oct): switch to `x: T` everywhere (closer to Scala/TS); record the style in docs/syntax.md. DeepSeek restyles .sw files, printer/messages, docs (not proposals/history), playground; hash_stability snapshots must not change.

tickets.title: AoC friction (days 2-4): parser, messages, proof ergonomics
tickets.body:
**AoC friction (days 2-4):** uppercase parameter names are a parse
error; error messages print fully evaluated terms (one was 10 KB); no type synonyms (`type Grid = List (List
Nat)` is a parse error; `def Grid : Type := ...` works); no
`List.zipWith3`; a multi-line list literal can't start a line with `,`;
char-pattern exhaustiveness error says "numbers other than 97 and 98";
no pair eta (`p = (p.fst, p.snd)` isn't `rfl`); recursive calls passed
as induction hypotheses must be fully applied; reasoning about `if` goes
through `Bool.inspect` with a hand-written motive; no `calc`/rewrite.

Split 19 Oct into SW-114, SW-115, SW-116. The `if` and calc items go to SW-26 and SW-99; pair eta is covered by SW-55 (its rewrite awaits Matt).

Closed 19 Oct (backlog review): fixed: type synonyms (a5ce8ce), `List.zipWith3` (prelude.sw:871), multi-line list starting with `,` (a5ce8ce), char-pattern exhaustiveness wording (a5ce8ce), `&&`/`||` (426b2b6, 02bf48d); the still-open items are split into new tickets.

tickets.title: Lambda postponing in effectful calls
tickets.where: Fixed by 6dc28126 (SW-223); cases added in examples/accept/lambda-postponed.sw
tickets.body:
Problem: a lambda argument whose parameter type is fixed by a later argument is postponed in pure calls (check.rs:903-970, examples/accept/lambda-postponed.sw), but not in effectful ones. Repro (type Person = { name: Text, age: Nat }):

    def appIO (f: a -> {IO} b) (x: a): {IO} b := f x
    def e1 (p: Person): {IO} Text := appIO (q => q.name) p
    -- E-CANNOT-INFER: can't tell what `q` is, so can't look up `.name`

The same call written with `appP` (no `{IO}` in the callback type) checks. A pure call placed after an effectful statement in the same block (`IO.print "x"` then `appP (q => q.name) p`) also fails. Cause (not yet confirmed): effectful calls apply arguments one at a time (crates/elab/src/effects.rs comp_call) and never go through apply_args_postponing.

First step: confirm the cause in effects.rs, then reuse the postponing path for calls whose arguments perform operations.

Done when: the repro above and a pure-after-effect variant check, with a test in examples/accept/ (extend lambda-postponed.sw) and the gate green.

History: was 'leave unless it bites'; reproduced 21 Oct. Related: SW-138 (done).

24 Oct 2026 (board review): both repros now check with a release binary built 24 Oct (appIO (q => q.name) p, and appP after an IO.print). The fixing commit is not identified (probably the effect-polymorphism row work, D1123/D1124, SW-406/SW-437). Remaining before closing: add the two cases to examples/accept/lambda-postponed.sw (neither is covered there), run the gate, then close.

tickets.title: Proof irrelevance (D1′): design decided
tickets.body:
**Two proofs of the same fact aren't treated as equal** (no definitional
proof irrelevance): `x % 100` with a hand-written divisor proof and
with the `auto` one have different types that print identically (Int
stage 6 worked around it with `[auto]` arguments). Consider proof
irrelevance for `Prop` in conversion (kernel; design note first).
Second example (19 Oct): char-pattern branches couldn't prove `c = 'a'`
because the matched char's validity proof differed from the literal's;
fixed in the elaborator with `Bool.uniqueEq` (`55c48eb`), which proof
irrelevance would make unnecessary. User (19 Oct): wants this considered, with the
literature and trade-offs properly understood: Opus design note after
multi-file Draft 3, with web research comparing at least Lean (definitional
irrelevance for `Prop`), Agda (opt-in `Prop`) and Coq/Rocq (`SProp`), and
the known metatheory (decidability, interaction with recursion on proofs,
large elimination, hashing).

Matt (19 Oct): adopt D1′; no Prop.irrel yet; remove canonical in stage 2; stage 3 on demand. Design done (draft 3, bf74b30).

tickets.title: `a_write_error_is_an_error`
tickets.body:
**`a_write_error_is_an_error`** (crates/cli/tests/run.rs) failed once
during a gate and passed on rerun: possibly flaky.

19 Oct: DeepSeek attempt stopped: OpenCode's sandbox refused reading outside the clone (Rust std source) and several shell commands; no reproduction recorded. Better suited to a Sonnet worktree lane (needs loops of the test binary and reading std's pipe code).

20 Oct 2026: failed again in the stage 2 gate (exit 0, expected 2), after SW-67 made runtime failures exit 2. Hypothesis (unverified): on macOS std creates pipes with a non-atomic close-on-exec, so a child spawned by a parallel test in the same binary can inherit the reader end; with a reader alive, the write succeeds. Fix idea: serialise child spawns in crates/cli/tests/run.rs with a static Mutex (or create the pipe via Command and drop the parent end), then loop the test binary to confirm.

tickets.title: Measure `textOfChars` in generated JS, then speed up `encodeChar` if it matters
tickets.body:
Generated JS turns a compact `List Char` into a string one character at a time: `textOfChars` (crates/js/src/lib.rs:890, emitted inside CHARS_OF_TEXT) loops `parts.push(encodeChar(l.head))`, and `encodeChar` (lib.rs:849) is `String.fromCodePoint(Number(v.code))`. The ticket author measured 98 ms per 10^6 characters (not re-measured in this review). Measure on a 10^6-character text under Node, profile, and decide whether a faster path is worth it (for example collecting code points and calling `String.fromCodePoint` in chunks, or skipping the `Number(...)` conversion).

Done when: a measured number is recorded in the ticket, and either a change that improves it measurably (with the extraction tests, crates/cli/tests/extract.rs, passing) or a 'not worth it' note.

History: the original said foldChars/compareChars were slow; they no longer exist.

tickets.title: Make `Def.body`/`Def.state` and `Data.state` private behind the admission API
tickets.body: crates/core/src/globals.rs:37-38 (`Def.body`, `Def.state`) and :100 (`Data.state`) are `pub`, so the elaborator and tests can bypass admission. Make them private and route writes through the admission API (kernel admission and mutual recursion are complete). Done: fields private, `cargo build` and the gate green.

tickets.title: More tail calls as loops in generated JS
tickets.body:
Only a function's calls to itself (including in either branch of a plain `if`) become loops today (self_tail_loop, crates/js/src/lib.rs:1430). A tail call inside `if h: P then a else b` is not recognised, because it is generated as `Decidable.elim … (v => a) (v => b)`; the same goes for helpers like `maybeThen`.

Repro (release binary, 21 Oct): scratch file
  def loopH (acc: Nat): Nat -> Nat
    | 0      => acc
    | Succ n => if h: n = 7 then acc else loopH (acc + 1) n
  export def count (n: Nat): Nat := loopH 0 n
built with `stitchwort build --js`; `count(1000000n)` throws `StitchwortResourceError: count: ran out of resources (Maximum call stack size exceeded)`. (The `if h:` here is a Decidable elimination, so the case tree does not see a tail position.)

First step: decide whether to treat `Decidable.elim` applications with lambda branches as an `if` in the tail analysis (crates/js/src/lib.rs:1617 `tail`) or to generate `if h:` as a conditional in the first place. Calls between different functions are SW-49.

Done when: the repro above, with 10^7 in place of 10^6, runs; an examples/extract file covers `if h:` in tail position.

tickets.title: JS codecs are about 2× slower on small inputs
tickets.body:
Problem: the generated-JS codecs (crates/js/src/lib.rs decoder around :980-1090, encoder) got about 2x slower on small inputs when they became iterative: a 5,000-element list took 0.3 ms before and 0.7 ms after, both ways. Not re-measured in this review.

First step: decide whether it matters (add a small-input case to the JS benchmark, crates/bench) and, if so, add a fast path for shallow values.

Done when: a benchmark row for small inputs exists and either the codecs are back near 0.3 ms or the ticket records that 0.7 ms is accepted.

History: 'if it matters'; relates to SW-38, SW-42 (JS codec measurements).

tickets.title: JS encoding doesn't preserve sharing
tickets.body:
A result with much sharing is encoded once per path: `echoTree(dag(12))` yields 2^13-1 objects (crates/cli/tests/extract.rs:775), so encoding a deeper DAG takes exponential time and memory. DESIGN.md:875 documents this as accepted; decoding already memoises shared nodes (DESIGN.md:850). Decide between: (a) memoise encoding per shared node, so the output shares objects too (what decoding does; cost: output objects are no longer a fresh tree, which a caller who mutates them could notice); (b) bound the output size and throw a clear `StitchwortResourceError` early; (c) leave as is. First step: choose, and update DESIGN.md:875 accordingly.

Done when: a test in crates/cli/tests/extract.rs encodes (or cleanly refuses) a DAG result of depth 60 quickly, and DESIGN.md:875 matches the behaviour.

History: found in the JS boundary work; accepted for the first milestone.

tickets.title: JS strings are checked at every place they appear
tickets.body:
Decoding scans a string each place it appears: the same 1 MB string in 1,000 slots is scanned 1,000 times (documented in DESIGN.md:875, 'Caveats'). Arrays and objects reached again by another path are decoded once (DESIGN.md:850, 'Shared parts are decoded once'); do the same for strings: remember the strings already validated in one decode, by identity.

First step: find the string validation in the decoder in crates/js/src/lib.rs (the string/Text decode near lines 865-910) and the shared-object table it can reuse; note a JS string has no identity, so the decision is what to key on (the string value itself costs a hash of the whole string, which is the same order as a scan: maybe only worthwhile for very long strings or via a length threshold).

Done when: a before/after measurement on the 1 MB string x 1,000 slots case is recorded in the ticket, and the DESIGN.md caveat is updated or removed. (If no identity-free scheme beats scanning, close with that measurement.)

tickets.title: Hostile Proxies at the JS boundary
tickets.body:
Problem: at the JS boundary the decoder's `Array.isArray(x)` and `x.length` (crates/js/src/lib.rs:1012-1015) run outside `own()` (:1032, :1056-1062, which wraps property reads), so a Proxy whose trap throws makes a raw exception escape instead of a boundary error.

First step: decide whether hostile inputs are in scope at all (the boundary already refuses non-plain data) or only containment of exceptions; the cheap fix is to run the whole decode in one try/catch that reports a boundary error.

Done when: a test passes a Proxy with throwing `get`/`has`/`getPrototypeOf` traps (and as an array element) and gets the normal boundary error, not the raw exception.

History: from the JS boundary work.

tickets.title: Support nested recursive types such as `List Tree` (rose trees)
tickets.body:
Nested recursive types are refused on purpose: `type Tree = | Node (kids: List Tree)` gives E-POSITIVITY ("`Tree` is used inside another type"), with the note to write a tree and a forest as a data group instead (verified on the release binary, 21 Oct). The rule is docs/core.md:101: `D` may appear in a field only as `D` applied to its own parameters, or as the result of a function field; nested occurrences like `List D` are rejected conservatively. Allowing them needs a design: positivity through type parameters (Lean's nested inductives, auxiliary-type compilation), what it does to termination (size change through `List.map`) and to JS extraction. The `rest : Nest (Box a)` form (non-uniform nesting) belongs to the same note.

First step: a design note (Opus, with external review, per the design-review gate) recommending build or don't build, with what mutual data groups (already implemented, examples/accept/mutual-data.sw) leave unsolved.

Done when: the note exists and Matt has decided build or not; if build, a follow-up implementation ticket is written.

History: the 'message half' (a clear E-POSITIVITY note) is fixed.

tickets.title: Mutual tail calls aren't loops in generated JS
tickets.body:
Mutual tail calls aren't loops in generated JS. Repro (checked 21 Oct with the release binary): `export def isEven: Nat -> Bool | 0 => True | Succ n => isOdd n` and `isOdd` the same the other way, built with `stitchwort build --js`, then `isEven(10000000n)` throws `StitchwortResourceError` (Maximum call stack size exceeded). The generated code is `const $Main$disEven = (v0) => { if (v0 === 0n) {...} else { const v1 = v0 - 1n; return $Main$disOdd(v1); } }` and the mirror image, so each call uses a JS stack frame. Self tail calls already become loops (SW-40 covers the remaining self-call cases); DESIGN.md:874 documents this limit.

First step: decide the approach. Options: (a) compile a group of mutually tail-calling functions into one loop with a state variable naming which member runs (no allocation; only works when every call between members is in tail position); (b) a trampoline for those calls (general but allocates a thunk per call); (c) leave it documented. Recommend (a) for groups where every inter-member call is a tail call, and (c) otherwise.

Done when: an extraction test in crates/cli/tests/extract.rs runs `isEven`/`isOdd` on 10000000n, and DESIGN.md:874 no longer lists `isEven`/`isOdd` as an example of overflow.

History: see SW-40 for self tail calls.

tickets.title: Mutual data types: members' parameters needn't be written identically
tickets.body:
In a group of mutual data types every member must spell its parameters the same, names included (docs/proposals/mutual-recursion.md:2163, 2269, 'Limits'). Allow renamed parameters (compare telescopes up to renaming).

First step: find where the group's parameter telescopes are compared (the mutual-data admission in crates/elab and the E-MUTUAL-* diagnostics) and decide the representation: rename each member's parameters to the first member's names before comparing.

History: split 19 Oct into SW-118 (JS error paths). Nested (`List Tree`) is SW-45; inductive-recursive and inductive-inductive types are documented out of scope, not tasks.

Done when: an examples/accept file whose members name the shared parameter differently is accepted, and an examples/reject one whose telescopes really differ is rejected with a clear message.

Merged into SW-77 (19 Oct)

tickets.title: `Term::Nat`'s hash doesn't include `Nat`'s own hash
tickets.body:
crates/core/src/hash.rs:486 hashes `Term::Nat` as the tag `nat` and the value only (`self.tag("nat"); self.nat(n)`), whereas `Term::Chars` (hash.rs:493) also hashes the `List` and `Char` data references it expands to (`self.data_ref(text.list)?; self.data_ref(text.char)?`). So changing `Nat`'s definition would not change the hash of a term that mentions a numeric literal. Include `Nat`'s own data reference in the `Term::Nat` hash, the way `Term::Chars` does it (take `Nat` from `self.g.builtins`). Hashes needn't stay stable (SW-32, no users yet); regenerate the snapshots and use them as the check that only the expected hashes moved.

Done when: `Term::Nat` hashes `Nat`'s reference, a unit test shows a different `Nat` definition gives a different hash for a literal, and the hash snapshots are regenerated (`git add` them) with `dev/t hashes` green.

History: found while reviewing the compact-text hashing.

tickets.title: JS internal-name encoding may collide
tickets.body:
**JS internal-name encoding may collide** (from reading the code, not
tested): a prime becomes `$` and a dot `$$`, and primes may appear
mid-name, so `a''b` and `a.b` both become `$a$$b`. Namespaces stage 1
added a new naming scheme with tests that names up to 4 characters are
distinct; check whether this item is now closed.

Closed 19 Oct (backlog review): 3faeb10 (namespaces stage 1): crates/js/src/lib.rs `encode` is written as injective (`'` -> `$p`, `.` -> `$d`, `%` -> `$g`, other `$uXXXXXX`; source names never contain `$`), so `a''b` (`a$p$pb`) and `a.b` (`a$db`) differ; field keys (`field_key`) likewise.

tickets.title: `==` operands are computed at check time
tickets.body:
**`==` operands are computed at check time.** `f x == y` puts `f x = y` in
a type, so checking computes `f x`. Needs lazily evaluated values, or a
translation of `==` that keeps its operands out of types.

Closed 19 Oct (backlog review): 65415c5 "Checker: decide with operands bound as variables, falling back to values (stage 1B)"; checker-evaluation.md "Stage 1B (done)": `cost == 5` 1,182,949 -> 23,225 steps. Residual (`if h : P` computing operands up to 3 times) is covered by SW-8.

tickets.title: Elaborating a chain is quadratic
tickets.body:
Elaborating a long chain is suspected to be quadratic: `Expr::span()` (crates/syntax/src/ast.rs:258) and `may_perform` (crates/elab/src/effects.rs:917) walk the whole subexpression at every level. Unverified: the first step is to measure (a chain of N `+` or applications, N = 1,000, 2,000, 4,000: time and a counter of nodes visited).

A regression guard needs a deterministic counter that these walks increment (the step/alloc counts of crates/bench don't see them); add one as part of the fix (from SW-35, 19 Oct: loops that neither evaluate nor allocate have no deterministic count).

Done when: the measurement is recorded; the walks are linear overall (cache the span, compute may_perform bottom-up); a bench row with the new counter guards it in bench/baseline.toml.

tickets.title: Performance of effectful code
tickets.body:
Effectful code is translated into `Effect.Comp` trees (docs/core.md:14), so a handler over a long computation walks a deep tree. No benchmark measures this: crates/bench/src/programs.rs has `run-prints` (20,000 `IO.print`s, :70) and `run-proof-fields` (:75), but no handler that threads state (a counter or a writer) through, say, 100,000 operations, and none in the checker. Add benchmark rows: (1) a state-handler loop of 10^5 operations through `stitchwort run` and through the evaluator, compared with the same loop written purely; (2) the same checked at type level where it applies. Record steps and time, and if a cost far above the pure version shows up, open a ticket for the cause.

Done when: the benchmark rows exist in crates/bench with a baseline (bench/baseline.toml), and the ticket records the ratio to pure code and whether a speed-up is warranted.

First step: decide how reachability is computed (rows after an all-variable row in the same column) in the number-pattern compile step in crates/elab (matching.rs).

tickets.title: Solving metavariables without recursion
tickets.body:
The elaborator's `solve`, `rename`, `prune` and `zonk` (zonk is at crates/elab/src/lib.rs:575) recurse over a solution. They're guarded, so a deep one gives E-RESOURCE, but they share the stack: `theorem a : [1, ..., n] = [1, ..., n] := Std.Eq.sym rfl` (hidden arguments solved to the list) checks at n = 20,000 and fails at n = 30,000 with `E-RESOURCE: the program is nested too deeply for the type checker` (reproduced 21 Oct, release binary); the original measurement was 56,875 with `rfl` and 26,875 with `sym rfl`. Bench rows `check-list-rfl` and `check-list-sym-rfl` (crates/bench/src/programs.rs:145-152) cover this. Also from SW-51: zonk walking computations inside types ran out of resources on `textJoin ... == t` with tens of thousands of characters; re-test it first, it may be gone after 65415c5.

Low priority: only large literal values in types hit it. Done when: the four passes use an explicit stack (or are shown not to need one), and `sym rfl` checks at least as far as `rfl` does (n = 56,875), with the benchmark rows updated.

tickets.body:
**A misleading follow-on error** (found by the IO lane): after an
`E-UNKNOWN-NAME` earlier in a file, a later `rfl` proof over a handled

Cause (inferred): greet failed, so the theorem's goal is stuck; the follow-on suppression near module.rs:328 misses this case. D18 (Matt): fix now, Sonnet lane.

tickets.title: The machine starts a nested machine
tickets.body:
The machine starts a nested machine when a native forces an argument that is a solved metavariable (elaboration only): natives call the public `force` (crates/core/src/native.rs:41, 427, 441), which enters a fresh machine. docs/proposals/stack-safe-evaluation.md:48 records this as the one exception to the 'no re-entry' rule (and :86, :253 state the rule). It is bounded by the term, not by program depth, so it is not a known failure; the cost is that the invariant 'a deep evaluation runs inside exactly one machine' (the test-only machine-entry counter, :253) has a hole.

First step: decide whether to close the hole or keep the exception. Option to close it: make the native return a request to force the metavariable as a machine state (as the `Apply` request does for `sub`, `leq`, `eqNat`), or make the elaborator zonk solved metas in the arguments before natives run. If neither is cheap, keep the exception and strengthen the note in stack-safe-evaluation.md with a depth bound.

Done when: either the machine-entry counter test passes for solved-metavariable arguments, or the doc states the bound and this ticket is closed as accepted.

History: stack-safe evaluation step 3.

tickets.title: Zero-argument effectful calls: `IO.readAllLines ()`
tickets.body:
Matt (19 Oct): how do Unison and other effect-tracking languages invoke 0-arity effectful actions, vs Stitchwort's `IO.readAllLines ()`? Research subagent (Sonnet, read-only): Stitchwort today, Unison/Koka/Effekt/Frank/Flix/Roc/OCaml 5/Scala/Haskell/Lean, options and a recommendation.

Research (Sonnet, 19 Oct): Stitchwort's 0-arity ops are `() -> {IO} T` thunks (prelude.sw:2236-2238), needed because evaluation is strict and effects happen at application (DESIGN.md:131-135). Strict effect languages call them with `f()` (Koka, Unison since UCM 0.5.23 alongside `!f`, Effekt, Flix, Scala's convention that `()` signals side effects); monadic languages (Haskell, Lean, Idris) make actions values, which in Stitchwort would expose `Comp` (abilities.md:259). Checked by Claude: `f()` and `def main(): {IO} ()` already parse and run. Recommendation: keep the unit-argument model; adopt `f()` / `def main()` (no space) as house style; `do e` sugar later; no `!` operator.

Matt (19 Oct): yes, adopt `f()` and `def main()` (no space) as house style via a DeepSeek restyle after the colon restyle (SW-24) lands; keep zero-argument actions as `() -> {IO} T` functions. `do e` sugar and a `!f` operator: not now.

Pure sugar, no soundness risk; the saving is five characters, so the case is weak. Not now (Matt).

Still missing: `(a % s + b) % s = (a + b) % s`, `a % s % s = a % s`, `Int.modNat (x + k * s) s = Int.modNat x s`, and `Int.modNat (x - 1)` for a position. With these, day 1's `backFrom`/`backFar` and the four `subNatNat` lemmas should go. Done: lemmas added; aoc/day01.sw simplified using them.

tickets.title: Proof by reflection: an arithmetic normaliser as an ordinary proof term (term-level `omega`)
tickets.body:
AoC proofs need hand-built arithmetic lemmas because the language has no `omega`/`ring` (docs/aoc-2025.md:96, :182); the day 1 comparison (docs/comparisons/aoc-day01.md, docs/compared.md:116 and :206) found Lean's `omega`, `simp` and `grind` roughly halved proof size. Stitchwort has no tactics, so the way to get such automation is proof by reflection: write an arithmetic normaliser (or a linear-arithmetic decision procedure) as an ordinary total function in the language, prove it sound once, and use it as a proof term (a term-level `omega`). Recommendation 4 from SW-96, large effort; `calc` and `rewrite` (docs/proposals/calc-rewrite.md, built) already give much of the benefit and are cheaper. Note Lean's `omega` can't do `/` or `%` by a variable either.

First step: a design note (Opus) scoping a fragment (for example linear `Nat`/`Int` equalities and inequalities over `+`, literal `*`, `<=`, `<`), the soundness proof it needs, and whether checking cost is acceptable given evaluator speed (docs/evaluator-speed.md).

Done when: the note exists with a build/don't-build recommendation and Matt has decided.

History: from SW-96 (day 1 comparison), recommendation 4.

tickets.title: Effectful callbacks for List.map / filter / folds
tickets.body:

Repro: `def p (xs: List Nat): {IO} List () := List.map (x => IO.print (Nat.toText x)) xs` gives E-ABILITY ('this may perform `IO`, which isn't allowed here').

Decide first: effect-polymorphic signatures (`(a -> {e} b) -> List a -> {e} List b`) versus separate effectful variants (`List.mapM`-style), and whether the pure uses keep elaborating identically (hashes aren't a constraint, but inference is). Check that existing inference of lambdas passed to `List.map` doesn't regress.

Done when: the repro checks and runs, and the gate (all existing List.map uses) is unchanged.

tickets.title: Termination: descend through record fields
tickets.body:
A recursive call on a field of a record parameter is refused today: matching a record binds its fields as `<` the parameter, `p.field` is a call of a generated definition (unknown for size change) and a rebuilt record is unknown, so `sum { list = Cons x xs, acc } = sum { list = xs, acc = acc + x }` is refused (docs/proposals/records.md:700-708). Implement the deferred design (records.md:709, decision R4 in the table at :163, section 7.5 at :1048): treat a known record parameter as its fields for size change, each a separate stable field path (`r.list`, `r.acc`), one layer deep, dependent fields as a telescope, and keep refusing `loop r = loop { r | list = r.list }` (a rebuilt record is not a descendant). The termination checker is crates/core/src/termination.rs.

Done when: examples are accepted and rejected as records.md section 6.4 and 7.5 say (an accept example for `sum` on a record, a reject example for the rebuilt-record loop), with unit tests, and records.md is updated from 'later' to 'as built'.

History: records design note; deferred from stages 1 and 2.

tickets.title: Dot notation sometimes elaborates differently from the prefix call
tickets.body:
Problem (reproduced 21 Oct): the dot form settles the receiver's literal type before the function's expected type is known:

    def c: List Int := [1, 2].map (x => x)           -- E-TYPE-MISMATCH: has type List Nat
    def d: List Int := List.map (x => x) [1, 2]      -- checks

Found converting examples to dot notation (SW-123): 14 conversions changed the elaborated term, e.g. `[True, False].map not`, `[1, 2].zip ...`, `.sort`/`.sortBy`/`.sortWith` in sort.sw, `.elem`/`.lookup` in list-toolkit.sw. docs/syntax.md:239 presents them as one call. Likely cause (inferred): the receiver is checked without the expected type (crates/elab/src/dot.rs), so a literal's type or an implicit is fixed as Nat, and evaluation order differs.

First step: print the elaborated terms for `c`/`d` and one of the hash-moving cases, then decide: make dot calls check the receiver against the expected result when the function is known, or document the difference in docs/syntax.md.

tickets.title: calc accepts a `<` chain against a `<=` goal when the sides compute to it; syntax.md:597 says the relation must match
tickets.body:
SW-157 pain point 10 (docs/aoc-2025.md:2068). Reproduced (21 Oct, release binary): `theorem t1 (a: Nat) (b: Nat) (h: a < Succ b): a <= b := calc a / _ < Succ b := h` (steps on separate lines) is accepted, while `calc a / _ < b := h` against `a <= b` gives E-CALC-GOAL ('the chain's relation is `<`, but the goal's is `<=`'). Cause: the goal check is by computation (syntax.md:597 'checked against it by computation'), and `a < Succ b` computes to `a <= b` (`Nat.leq (Succ a) (Succ b)` reduces to `Nat.leq a b`), so the check passes by conversion, not by weakening. It is harmless and handy; `rangeEnd` (aoc/src/Aoc/Common/Proofs/Range.sw:9) relies on it.

Decide: (a) document it (change syntax.md:597 from 'its relation must be the goal's' to say that a relation which computes to the goal's is accepted, with this example and a test in examples/accept/calc.sw), or (b) make it an error (compare the relation syntactically before conversion). Recommend (a): (b) adds a special case and breaks `rangeEnd`.

Done when: the decision is recorded and either syntax.md and examples/accept/calc.sw match the behaviour, or the error exists with a reject example.

tickets.title: Derived == for indexed families (parked until a program needs it)
tickets.body:
Derived `==` (DecEq) refuses types with indices (crates/elab/src/derive.rs:214-217, 'has indices, which … isn't derived for yet') and handles only fields whose types don't depend on earlier fields (derive.rs:10-15). Families like `VCons [n := m] x (xs: Vec a m)` need dependent injectivity projections, index-generic tag/differ helpers and a J-based proof carrying index unification (>300 lines).

Options: (1) only families whose fields don't depend on implicit fields; (2) full dependent derivation; (3) leave it. Fin's `FSucc [n := j] (i: Fin j)` has a dependent field, so option 1 doesn't cover Fin.

History: bug sweep 21 Oct 2026. Parked (Claude, 21 Oct): Vec has a library DecEq (Vec.sw:115) and Fin has a hand-written instance (SW-191, done), so the library needs nothing; revisit when a program needs `==` on a user-defined family. First step then: choose among the options.

def half (n: Nat): Maybe Nat := match n with | Zero => Nothing | Succ k => Just k
def Small (n: Nat): Maybe Nat -> Prop | Nothing => Unit | Just k => And (k < n) Unit
theorem halfSmall (n: Nat): Small n (half n) := match n with | Zero => Trivial | Succ k => Both (Nat.leRefl (Succ k)) Trivial
theorem useLet (n: Nat): Nat.leq 0 n = True :=
  let small := halfSmall n
  match e: half n with | Nothing => rfl | Just k => match small with | Both a b => rfl

type Hit = { row: Nat, column: Nat }
def paths (r: Nat) (c: Nat): List Bool -> List (List Hit)
  | Nil => [Nil]
  | Cons b rest =>
    if b then
      List.append
        (match c with
           | Zero => [[{ row = r, column = c }]]
           | Succ k => (paths (r + 1) k rest).map (Cons { row = r, column = c }))
        ((paths (r + 1) (c + 1) rest).map (Cons { row = r, column = c }))
    else paths (r + 1) c rest

tickets.title: calc: a first expression containing `||` or `&&` needs parentheses
tickets.body:
SW-157 pain point 6 (docs/aoc-2025.md:2051). Reproduced (21 Oct, release binary): `theorem t (a: Bool) (b: Bool): a || b = b || a := calc a || b` with the step `_ = b || a := Bool.orComm a b` on the next line gives E-PARSE 'expected a step `_ = e` on the next line, indented past `calc`, but found `||`' pointing at the `||` on the calc line, with the note 'a `calc` needs at least one step'; the same happens for a step's expression. `+` and `*` are fine. The parser reads the first expression of a `calc` before it knows an operator may continue it (crates/syntax/src/parser.rs, `starts_calc_step` :330 is the nearby logic). Either parse a full expression after `calc` and in steps, or make the message say to write `(a || b)`.

tickets.title: match generalisation surprises: branch goals computed one step, `Decidable.toBool` leaks, E-MATCH-MOTIVE on `match h: a <= b`
tickets.body:
SW-157 pain points 3, 4 and 5 (docs/aoc-2025.md:2033-2050), all about `match` generalising more than the scrutinee you see. (3) A branch's goal has already computed one step (syntax.md's 'branch goals have already computed one step'), so a proof written for the original goal doesn't fit (`termsSum`/`twiceTerms`, `coveredTop`). (4) Generalising leaks `Decidable.toBool (Bool.decTrue (Nat.leq id (hi r)))` into messages where `Nat.leq id (hi r) = False` was written; the workaround is the lemma `Bool.decTrueToBool` (`x <= y` as a `Bool` should print and compute as `Nat.leq`). (5) `match h: a <= b with` can give E-MATCH-MOTIVE ("generalising this `match`'s scrutinee makes its type ill-formed") while `match h: Nat.leq a b with` is fine, and the message doesn't say which form to use.

Not re-verified in this review (the AoC files they cite have since been restructured). First step: write a minimal example for each of the three on current main, then decide per item: fix, or improve the message/doc.

tickets.title: rewrite diagnostics: E-REWRITE-NOTHING after `%` and `/` unfold, and an unreadable E-REWRITE-BUDGET term
tickets.body:

The computed goal in the note made each quick to fix, so the improvement is to say in the message that the goal is searched after computation. (8) `E-REWRITE-BUDGET` shows an unreadable term when the rule is closed and big; the per-declaration time report that would have found the slow `rewrite` at once is SW-163 and is not part of this ticket.

tickets.title: Two instances with the same name panic the elaborator (index out of bounds, crates/elab/src/module.rs:1177)
A cycle between a type's constructor and a later declaration gives E-INTERNAL 'is used before it's checked'
tickets.body:
Found by the SW-685 elaborator fuzzer (oracle 2, no E-INTERNAL). Seeds/cases: default 0x5eede1ab00000685 case 5981 (accept/quot-forms.sw); 0x2 case 3085 (accept/index-proof-conflict-data.sw); 0xabcdef cases 568 and 1084. All the same shape after reduction: a type's constructor (or an index type) names a later declaration that in turn names the type, so the declarations form a cycle the order check doesn't catch. Minimal input:

def Q: Type := List T
type T: Q → Type =
  | A: T Nil

gives '[E-INTERNAL] internal error: `Q` is used before it's checked', 'this is a bug in the compiler'. Variants: 'type Vec (a: Type): Nat → Type = | VCons (x: a) (xs: Vec a n): Box a (Succ n)' followed by 'type Box: Type 1 = | Mk [a: Type] (xs: List a) (rest: Vec)' (E-INTERNAL on Box); a theorem 'noAB: SameP A B → Void' used by an earlier type's constructor and mentioning that type (E-INTERNAL on noAB). Expected: an ordinary cyclic-dependency error (the code for mutually recursive declarations that aren't declared together) at the use.

tickets.title: Kernel's E-TYPE-MISMATCH reaches the user for a Comp whose result row is an unbound variable (elaborator lets an ill-typed term through)
tickets.body:
Found by the SW-685 elaborator fuzzer (oracle 3, the kernel never rejects an elaborated term; seed 0x1 case 1633, from reject/empty-row-function.sw). Minimal input:

import Std.Effect (Comp, NoOp)
def next (n: Nat): Comp NoOp r Nat := n + 1

The error ('[E-TYPE-MISMATCH] type mismatch ... expected Comp Effect.NoOp r Nat, but this has type Comp Effect.NoOp Effect.NoRes Nat') is the kernel's, not the elaborator's: stitchwort_elab::take_kernel_rejections (the hook SW-685 adds in crates/elab/src/kernel.rs) records the same message from a define call. So the elaborator accepted `n + 1` against a type with an auto-bound variable `r` (it should have reported the mismatch itself, or failed to unify NoRes with the rigid `r`). Severity is low: the user still gets a reasonable error, only from the wrong layer. The fuzzer oracle flags any kernel E-MALFORMED/E-TYPE-MISMATCH/E-NOT-A-* whose message reaches the user unchanged.

tickets.title: Memory blow-up: List.Mem hypothesis + failing proof + Vec-nested type
tickets.body:
`check --no-cache` on this file goes past 28 GB in about 8 s (found by the SW-704 stage 3 lane). It happens on main too: the binary built from main 82729c37 was killed by dev/memguard at 3.17 GB against a 2 GB cap (checked by the orchestrator on 30 Oct). So it isn't caused by stage 3.

    import Std (List, Nat, Vec)
    type Packet: Type = | Number (value: Nat) | Packets (items: List Packet)
    theorem smaller (items: List Packet) (q: Packet) (h: List.Mem q items): q = q := nope
    type Wide: Type = | WLeaf | WNode (kids: Vec Wide 2)

The lane found that all three parts are needed: removing `Wide`, removing `h`, or giving a working proof makes it fine. Not investigated beyond that. Always run repros under dev/memguard --cap-gb 2.

Investigation (30 Oct, lane worktree-agent-a41739081c8754ea3):
- Smaller repro, no `h`, no `Wide`, no Vec: `type Rose: Type = | Leaf | Node (kids: List Rose)` with `theorem t (q: Rose): q = q := nope`. Killed by memguard at 3.05 GB after 1.0 s CPU.
- `sample` shows 712 of 737 samples in `counterexample::search_counterexample`, inside a deep recursion of `Inputs::random` (List branch) under `Inputs::random_tuple`.
- Cause: in crates/elab/src/counterexample/inputs.rs:714-716, a random `List` gets a length of up to `size`, and every element is drawn at the full `size` again. For a rose tree this grows faster than exponentially. Debug counter: the biggest tuple per size was 4063 nodes at size 12, 134260 at 15, 466313 at 16 and 2942245 at 17, while sizes go up to RANDOM_SIZE = 40. MAX_DEPTH bounds only the depth, not the width. mod.rs:540-548 builds all the random tuples before any time check.
- Why the three parts: a failing proof (any failing proof, `:= h` too, not only an unknown name) runs the search (module.rs:580). `h: List.Mem q items` puts the theorem out of scope ("nothing decides List.Any") unless List.decMem is loaded, and any use of Vec (even `def foo: Vec Nat 0 := Vec.VNil`) loads it. So `Wide` matters only because it uses Vec. Removing `h` doesn't make it go away when `items` stays. Declaration order doesn't matter.
- Not related to derive_induct.rs or size_from_member.
- Experiment (debug commit 8b5cbbea): give each list element `size / length`. The repro then finishes in 0.14 s CPU with at most 64 nodes per tuple, and d9.sw checks in 0.83 s.
Fix lane (30 Oct, worktree-agent-acfd19afe8504e35e): list and Vec elements share the size (size / length), MAX_RANDOM_VALUES = 1000 per draw, drawing stops at the random phase's time; Rose repro 3 GB-killed -> 0.15 s CPU (1b571d5c). Next: examples, snapshots, docs.
Fix lane done (30 Oct): commits 1b571d5c (fix), 9c8f91f2 (example reject/counterexample-nested-trees.sw + driver test), 39805dec (docs). No existing snapshot changed (task snap:examples). Lane elab 78/78, examples NAME=counterexample 7/7, core 153/153, driver counterexamples 22/22; clippy, fmt clean. Ready for the merge tier.

tickets.title: SOUNDNESS: universe level overflow, Type 4294967295 : Type 0 is accepted
tickets.body:
SOUNDNESS. Found 30 Oct 2026 by the kernel-bug test lane (kernel register T1, porting Lean's looseBVarRange bit-overflow shape); reproduced by the orchestrator with main's release binary.

`def wrap: Type 0 := Type 4294967295` is ACCEPTED ("checked"). So is `def wrap2: Type 4294967295 := Type 4294967294`. (`def big: Type 4294967295 := Nat` is rightly E-UNIVERSE; `Type 4294967296` is E-PARSE "universe level is too large".)

Cause: universe levels are u32 (`crates/core/src/term.rs:24`, `Sort::Type(u32)`), and the step to the next universe adds one unchecked: the kernel's `Sort::succ` (`term.rs:32`, `Sort::Type(i) => Sort::Type(i + 1)`, used at `crates/core/src/check.rs:286` and `:608`) and the elaborator (`crates/elab/src/check.rs:1218`). Release builds have no overflow checks (no `overflow-checks` in Cargo.toml), so `Type u32::MAX : Type 0`. The parser accepts any level that fits in a u32 (`crates/syntax/src/parser.rs:3882`).

Consequence: the universe hierarchy is cyclic (Type 0 : ... : Type u32::MAX : Type 0), the setting of Girard's/Hurkens' paradox, so a proof of Void should be constructible (not built; treat as unsound). Also `Sort::fits_in` (term.rs:53-58) lets a Type 0 data type hold a field of type Type u32::MAX.

Fix direction: the kernel must refuse a universe whose successor doesn't exist (checked add, an error rather than saturating, since Type MAX : Type MAX is just as bad), the elaborator likewise, and the parser should keep levels far below the limit. Then audit the kernel for other unchecked arithmetic on levels, de Bruijn indices or counters. Must-reject tests for both programs above.


30 Oct (fix lane): reproduced on main release: wrap, wrap2 and a Type 0 data type with a `Type 4294967295` field are all "checked". Plan: MAX_LEVEL = 65535 (u16::MAX), checked Sort::succ in kernel and elab, parser limit, cache read limit.
30 Oct (fix lane): fix committed on branch (e1d444d7 kernel, da80af16 parser/elab/cache, d8d36404 examples); repros now E-PARSE / E-UNIVERSE; hashes lane unchanged. Next: audit, docs, lanes.
30 Oct (fix lane): done on branch worktree-agent-a00641332c276221f (e1d444d7, da80af16, d8d36404, d3c2dee4). Lanes core 160, elab 78, syntax 170, examples 7, std 21, hashes 3 all pass; hashes unchanged; clippy, fmt clean. overflow-checks=true on aoc check: no difference above noise (user median 41.1 s main, 39.4 s with checks, 40.6 s branch, loaded machine). tickets.title: Panic 'internal error: applying a constructor' (value.rs:815) in dev search matching std theorem pairs
tickets.where: fixed (939c66a8): E-TYPE-MISMATCH instead of panic; search panics 80-91 -> 0-3
tickets.body:
Found by the SW-915 search lane (30 Oct 2026). `stitchwort dev search 'self:conclusion'` (docs/proposals/search/queries-draft2.sh, section self) panics with "internal error: applying a constructor" (crates/core/src/value.rs:815, the catch-all in apply) on 4 pairs of std theorems with the constants filter and 12 without, e.g. the pattern from `Std.Parse.runFromMark` against `Std.Parse.runFromNatThere` (docs/proposals/search.md §6.1, stage S1a).

Not yet known: whether this is reachable from ordinary elaboration, or only from search's matching (which unifies a pattern with theorem types it hasn't type-checked against, so an ill-typed meta solution could put a constructor in head position). First step: reduce the pair to a minimal repro, then decide whether the fix is in search (check types before unifying) or in unify/eval. A panic in core is a bug either way; it should be an error, not a crash.

30 Oct (lane): reachable from ordinary `stitchwort check`, not search-only. Minimal repro (panics at value.rs:815 under plain `check`; backtrace effects::pure_let -> quote_folded -> force_solved -> apply_step):

    def app [p: Bool → Type] (x: p True): p True := x

    def probe (t: (Nat → Nat) → Type) (mk: (g: Nat → Nat) → t g) (use: (g: Nat → Nat) → t g → g 0 = g 0): Nat :=
      let e := use _ (app (mk _))
      let f: 1 = 1 := e
      0

Cause: unify.rs `first_order`. Checking `mk ?g : t ?g` against `?p True`: `?p True` isn't a pattern (True isn't a variable), so first_order pairs the last arguments, `True =?= ?g`, and solves `?g : Nat → Nat` with `True` (logged: `solve ?g := x x x => True`). Its doc comment says "the kernel re-checks the result", but the elaborator evaluates `?g 0` (from `g 0 = g 0`) before any re-check, and applying `True` panics. With `use` returning `Nat` instead, the same file gives a clean E-TYPE-MISMATCH ("`True` builds a `Bool`, but the expected type is `Nat → Nat`").

Search pair (runFromMark against runFromNatThere): same mechanism. Logged solutions: pattern `?k (?s.at)` against target `Effect.bind (Parse.nat.%match1 …) k'`; first_order gives `?k := Effect.bind (Parse.nat.%match1 …)` and `k' := Parse.State.at ?s` (a Mark record, where k' : Nat → {Parse} a). A postponed comparison (unify::run, Task::Later) then re-quotes and applies it. Search only makes such ill-typed pairings more common.

The fix belongs in unify.rs (first_order mustn't pair last arguments of different types, or a solution must be checked before use). Stopped per the lane brief, since the postponement stage 6 lane is rewriting the unifier. No commits.



30 Oct (orchestrator): repro verified on main: plain `stitchwort check` on the 6-line file panics at value.rs:815. So this is an elaborator bug, not search-only: `first_order` (unify.rs) solves `?g: Nat → Nat` with `True` from `True =?= ?g` when `?p True` isn't a pattern, and the elaborator evaluates `?g 0` before the kernel re-check. A crash, not a false theorem (the kernel still re-checks). Fix belongs in unify.rs (don't pair last arguments of different types, or check a solution's type before use; `can_apply` in `push_eta` is a partial guard). Waits for postponement stage 6 (SW-817), which is rewriting the unifier; then a lane fixes it with the repro as a reject example. Core's panic arm left as is: turning it into an error needs a new eval error kind, since callers read eval errors as budget errors.


D2075 (Matt, 31 Oct 2026): one unifier lane, SW-919 first then SW-920, separate commits.

31 Oct (unifier lane, 939c66a8 on worktree-agent-aeeef626c57618f7d): fixed in the unifier. Unknowns record their type where whoever makes them knows it (a hole checked against a type, an implicit or `auto` argument, search's opened binders: `Meta::ty`). `first_order` refuses to pair the last arguments (or the rest) when their types are known to differ in outermost form (`apart`, by `rigid_head` without type variables). Repro: panic -> E-TYPE-MISMATCH (`reject/unify-last-arguments-types-differ.sw`); unit test in unify.rs. Hashes: std+aoc and std+rogue dumps byte-identical. Search panics, queries-draft3.sh, base -> lane: conclusions 4,4,4,4,12 -> 0,0,0,0,0; left sides 2,2,2,2,12 -> 0,0,0,0,7; uses 18,80,80,78,79,91 -> 0,1,1,1,0,3. The 7 left-side panics left (filter:off) are a different one, value.rs:1621: a case meets a constructor of another type, e.g. Nat.compareFlip's left side (an Ordering) against Bool.xorAssoc's (a Bool). [Inferred: search compares sides of different types, which no guard in first_order can make well-typed; the uses ones not examined.]

tickets.title: Unifier: identity shortcut doesn't see through solved unknowns (modLt against % 2^31: 24.7 s)
tickets.body:
Split from SW-917 (30 Oct 2026). The slowdown happens without `rewrite`: `Std.Nat.modLt (_ * 1103515245 + 12345) 2147483648` checked against a transparent `(seed * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648 < 2147483648` takes 24.7 s and 154M steps (quadratic in the added constant: `Nat.mod` unfolds `Nat.divFuel` once per `Succ` of `+ 12345`).

Cause found by the SW-917 lane: the identical-closure shortcut (`same_closure`, unify.rs Lam case ~936, via `value::identical`, crates/core/src/value.rs ~3393) compares heads without forcing solved unknowns, so `Meta(?x)` (solved to `seed`) against `Var(seed)` counts as different and unify descends into two equal terms structurally. The `Nat.div` call shortcut misses because its arguments solve the `auto ok` proof.

Likely fix: make the identity shortcut see through solved unknowns (substitute before comparing, or retry identity after forcing). Touches unify.rs / core `identical`, so wait until postponement stage 6 (SW-817) has merged; then re-measure, since stage 6 may change these paths. Hash changes possible; must be explained.


D2075 (Matt, 31 Oct 2026): one unifier lane, SW-919 first then SW-920, separate commits.

31 Oct (unifier lane, 3ffe8f83 on worktree-agent-aeeef626c57618f7d): fixed. Unification's two identity shortcuts (Lam pairs and codomains) use core's new `same_closure_solved`: where two values differ as they are and one is headed by a solved unknown, they're compared again with the solution applied (a cold path, reached only on a mismatch). The kernel's `same_closure` is unchanged. Repro: elaboration 23,900 ms -> 0.5 ms; work 155,038,533 -> 528,572 steps (prelude included; with `seed` written: 528,513). Test `conv_shortcut::a_solved_unknown_is_seen_through_by_the_identity_shortcut` bounds the `_` version's work by the `seed` version's +10% (fails at 155M without the fix; added to lane-elab), plus a core unit test. tickets.title: R4 (SW-787) makes x % D with a + K literal unfold Nat.divFuel K levels: huge normal forms (Float.Theory magUnits*, lcg), slow unification (SW-920)
tickets.where: stage 1 merged (P1); stage 2 / SW-554 later (D2081); bench times need re-recording on a quiet machine
tickets.body:
Found while getting the full tier green (31 Oct 2026; differential test fix 817c3ad7). Since 1ed90886 (SW-787, R4: `+` also computes on its second argument), `x + K` with a literal K normalises to `Nat.add K x`-style forms that hand known fuel to recursions such as `Nat.divFuel`. So `m % D` or `m / D` where m contains `+ K` and an unknown unfolds `divFuel` up to K levels, each stuck on the unknown with the next inside it: the normal form grows with K (measured for small K = 4, 8, 16, 32: 1.6k, 4.1k, 11.9k, 37.6k characters, faster than linear).
Where it bites today:
- std Float.Theory `magUnitsFieldNext`, `magUnitsWholeAt`, `magUnitsWhole`, `magUnitsCarry` (types about `magUnits (e * 2^52 + 2^52 + …)`, `magUnits m = Nat.divFuel m m 2^52`): quoting a type passes 4 GB; the reference `conv` overflows.
- examples/accept/partial-handlers.sw `lcg seed = (seed * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2^31`: normal forms over 4 GB; two closed tests take ~55 s in conversion.
- SW-920 (unifier `modLt` against `% 2^31`, 24.7 s) and SW-917 (rewrite, fixed separately) are the same unfolding.
These are left out of the differential test for now. Not yet decided: whether R4 should stop handing literal fuel to such recursions (e.g. don't commute when the result feeds a fuel argument, a fuel-free Nat.div/mod (SW-554), or lazy unfolding), measured on std/AoC/rogue. Inferred, not tested: these passed before 1ed90886.


D2077 (Matt, 31 Oct 2026): design lane. Compare the fix options (1) a division that does not step through the number one unit at a time (SW-554), (2) narrowing R4, (3) lazier unfolding; measure each on std, AoC and rogue; and compare what other languages in our space do for Nat division/mod (definitions, kernel/native support, reduction behaviour) and how well they handle this case compared to us. Design note before any code.

31 Oct (design lane): reproduced: normal form of (x*3+K)/2^31 is 355, 29.8k, 438k, 6.9M, 27.4M chars at K = 4, 64, 256, 1024, 2048 (41 s), E-RESOURCE at 4096. Prototype P1 (divFuel's step takes the comparison as its first argument, so a stuck step stays folded; natives unchanged): 132 chars at K = 12345; SW-920 repro 29.8 s -> 0.21 s; std 2328, aoc 1363, rogue 190 theorems pass, two std lemma statements changed; differential test passes partial-handlers and float-playlist with the R4 exclusions removed. Lean, Agda, Rocq, Idris run; note next.

31 Oct (design lane): note docs/proposals/division.md on branch worktree-agent-aa5219c3981af5a43 (768497c8; prototype bf47f1d3, reverted ad6bcb34). Others: Agda/Rocq count down the dividend with a counter (small stuck term); Lean and Idris 2 use our fuel scheme (Lean hides it with irreducible; forced, worse than ours); Agda running our divFuel blows up as we do. Option (b) (R4 only up to 64) breaks Float.Theory.keyHigh. P1 merge tier: 906/911, the 5 are hash snapshots plus Nat.toText's runtime native dropping off its pinned hash (re-pin in stage 1). Rec: P1 as stage 1, keep R4. Open: D2080-D2082.

tickets.title: A match's motive check is skipped when its scrutinee holds an unsolved unknown (E-MATCH-MOTIVE missed)
tickets.body:
Found by the D2086 design lane (SW-817), 31 Oct 2026, on main 8b75b5c7 [run].

A `match` on an expression checks that generalising its scrutinee keeps every type well formed (`check_motive`, crates/elab/src/matching.rs:765-766). When the scrutinee still holds an unsolved unknown, building that type fails ("can't work out an implicit argument") and the check is skipped: "something isn't known yet: checked when it's admitted". But the helper is admitted with only the variables its body uses, so a generalised hypothesis the body doesn't use is never checked.

Repros (docs/proposals/postponement/, added by the D2086 design commit):
- motive-field-later.sw: `apply (r => match List.length [r.x, r.x] with ...) p` with `q: two 2 rfl b = 2` in scope; `r.x` waits for `r`'s type (stage 2's K2). Accepted. The same with `(r: P)` is E-MATCH-MOTIVE.
- motive-param-later.sw: `match List.length [r] with ...`, `r` a lambda parameter of unknown type (an ordinary unknown, no queue item). Accepted; the annotated twin is E-MATCH-MOTIVE.

Fix (D2086 design, "Stage 4: design for the third attempt" in docs/proposals/postponement.md): the check doesn't skip; the match waits for the unknowns its generalisation reads (a queue item, scrutinee kept as a term), so the motive is checked once they are known. Step 4.0 of the third attempt; can land before K4.
